stem: A candidate with alcohol-related liver disease asks how long many U.S. programs require abstinence before liver transplant waitlist placement. Which counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Many programs require about six months of abstinence before waitlist placement
Active alcohol use is encouraged until the day of transplant
Abstinence is never required for any liver transplant candidate
A ten-year abstinence period is required by every program without exception

explanation.rationale_correct: In the United States, many transplant programs require six months of abstinence before a patient can be placed on the liver transplant waiting list, although protocols vary by center.

rationale_incorrect.B: Alcohol abstinence is required for liver transplant candidacy rather than continued use until surgery.
rationale_incorrect.C: Abstinence requirements are commonly applied for alcohol-related liver disease.
rationale_incorrect.D: References describe a common six-month requirement, not a universal ten-year mandate.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 12, Liver Transplantation → alcoholic liver disease → listing requirements
primary_anchor.quote_hint: many transplant programs require 6 months of abstinence before a patient can be placed on the liver transplant waiting list

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 12 → alcoholic liver disease listing (many programs require 6 months abstinence before waitlist placement); PDF p. 644 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 010200 item; liver alcohol-abstinence angle distinct from smoking contraindications (cctc-1034/1037) and obesity (cctc-1050); anchor verified on Cupples p. 644.

stem: During early post-transplant education, a heart recipient asks when they may resume lifting grandchildren. Which activity guidance aligns with standard references?

options.text: Lifting items greater than about 5 to 10 pounds may be restricted during early recovery
No lifting restrictions apply at any time after transplant
Only recipients over age 80 have lifting restrictions
Lifting restrictions apply only before transplant, never afterward

explanation.rationale_correct: Early post-transplant lifestyle teaching may include activity restrictions such as lifting any item greater than 5 to 10 pounds, along with restrictions on tub soaking, swimming, hot tubs, contact sports, and driving until team reassessment.

rationale_incorrect.B: Early recovery commonly includes lifting restrictions rather than unrestricted activity immediately.
rationale_incorrect.C: Lifting restrictions are described for early post-transplant recovery broadly, not a single age threshold.
rationale_incorrect.D: Post-transplant activity restrictions apply during early recovery after surgery.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → g. Lifestyle changes → i. Potential activity restrictions

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → g. Lifestyle changes → i. Potential activity restrictions (lifting >5–10 lb and related limits); PDF p. 110 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Twelfth 010500 item; heart activity-restriction angle distinct from insulin teaching (cctc-1055) and travel restriction (cctc-1025); anchor verified on Cupples p. 110.

stem: A coordinator is updating early post-transplant infection-prevention and lifestyle teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Soaking in a tub, swimming, and using a hot tub may be restricted early after transplant.
Contact sports may be restricted during early recovery.
Driving may resume immediately on discharge without transplant team reassessment.
Walking and activities of daily living are encouraged when appropriate.

explanation.rationale_correct: Early lifestyle teaching includes restrictions on tub soaking, swimming, hot tubs, and contact sports, while encouraging walking and activities of daily living; driving is prohibited until the patient is reassessed by the transplant team.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—walking and activities of daily living are encouraged.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statements I and II are also true; statement III is false because driving requires team reassessment.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false; driving is not permitted immediately without reassessment.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → g. Lifestyle changes
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Soaking in a tub or swimming and using a hot tub … Contact sports … Driving will be prohibited until … reassessed … walking and activities of daily living

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → g. Lifestyle changes (tub/swimming/hot tub limits, contact sports, driving prohibition, encouraged walking/ADLs); PDF p. 110 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Synthesized item. Fourteenth complex_combo in bank; distinct from dietary combo (cctc-1052) and hot-tub single item (cctc-1053); anchor verified on Cupples p. 110.

stem: Before discharging a living liver donor, which topic should the coordinator verify is included in donor education per standard references?

options.text: Activity restrictions including lifting, exercise, travel, and return to work
No follow-up is ever required after living donation
Donors should ignore fever or uncontrolled pain rather than calling the team
Wound assessment and when to call the living donor team are unnecessary

explanation.rationale_correct: Living liver donor discharge teaching includes activity restrictions such as lifting, exercise, travel, and return to work, along with wound assessment and parameters for contacting the living donor team.

rationale_incorrect.B: Follow-up appointments and instructions are part of living donor discharge teaching.
rationale_incorrect.C: Donors should call the living donor team for fever, uncontrolled pain, shortness of breath, or other concerns.
rationale_incorrect.D: Wound assessment and team contact instructions are required discharge education elements.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 7, Living Donation → E. Discharge Teaching → 2.b.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Activity restrictions including lifting, exercise, travel, and return to work

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
